name: Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition

Optimal.Notes: Native 1280x800 with medium-high settings delivers a sharp, stable experience that suits the game's art style; the 10 W TDP cap keeps thermals and fan noise comfortable during long sessions. This is the sweet spot most Deck players will enjoy.

profiles.Summary: Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition runs well on the Steam Deck under Proton, with gold-tier ProtonDB reports confirming solid playability; the main challenge is the small UI and text at 1280x800, which the game partially addresses with its adjustable text size feature. The game's modest PC requirements sit comfortably within the Deck's capabilities, allowing stable 60 fps at medium-to-high settings without heavy power draw.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck configuration reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's modest PC minimum/recommended requirements (GTX 650-class GPU target) compared to the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU, which comfortably exceeds those targets. On your first run, check frame rate during a large multiplayer or late-game battle — if it dips below your cap, lower Shadow Quality and Terrain Quality first.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 and a 6 W TDP cap dramatically extends battery life; the game's 2D-heavy art style holds up well at lower render resolution. Increase UI Scale in-game to keep the HUD readable.

KnownIssues: UI elements and minimap can be very small at native 1280x800 — use the in-game UI scale and adjustable text size settings to compensate.
Mouse-driven RTS controls are awkward without a keyboard/mouse; consider using the Deck's trackpads and back buttons with a custom controller layout.
Online multiplayer cross-play sessions may occasionally require additional Proton compatibility steps or show connectivity issues under some network conditions.
Some users report minor stutters during large-battle scenarios with many units on screen simultaneously.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Max settings at native resolution are well within the Deck's GPU headroom for this older-engine title; uncapped at 15 W, the game holds 60 fps in most scenarios but large late-game battles with hundreds of units may dip to the mid-50s. Battery life is short at full TDP, so plug in for long sessions.

Optimal.Notes: Rendering at 1152x720 with mild FSR upscaling delivers a sharp, clean image at 60 fps for most gameplay situations. This is the sweet spot for campaign and multiplayer sessions with good battery life.

profiles.Summary: Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition runs well on the Steam Deck via Proton, with the game's modest GPU requirements making it a comfortable fit for the hardware even at higher settings. Being a real-time strategy title with a largely 2D/3D hybrid engine, it is not GPU-bound but can be CPU-intensive in late-game scenarios with many units on screen.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's modest PC requirements (well below Deck-class GPU), its 2D/3D hybrid RTS engine, and the Gold ProtonDB tier. On first run, check frame rates during a large late-game battle — that is the most demanding scenario — and drop to Optimal if you see sustained drops below 50 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a low TDP cap keeps the APU cool and the battery lasting through long campaign sessions. Late-game battles may dip slightly but the 40 fps cap keeps things stable.

KnownIssues: UI text and interface elements can be very small at native resolution without accessibility scaling adjustments — use the in-game Adjustable Text Size feature.
Controller/gamepad support is limited; a keyboard-and-mouse or touchpad + touchscreen setup is strongly recommended for comfortable play.
Late-game scenarios with large armies and many units can cause CPU-related frame drops.
No native Linux build; runs through Proton, which is generally stable at Gold tier but occasional multiplayer connectivity issues have been noted.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At full native resolution with all settings maxed, the Deck's GPU is well within its comfort zone for this engine and can push high frame rates — though late-game 200-unit battles may pull this down to the 60s. Battery life will be short at full TDP.
